title: L3: Conclude severe (exponential) ill-posedness from the bound

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Goal.** Convert the upper bound of the crux lemma into the dichotomy answer and the severe/exponential label.

(a) *Disprove moderate ill-posedness.* From $\sigma_i(A)=o(i^{-\kappa})$ for every $\kappa$, conclude there is NO pair $(C,\kappa)$ with $C\,i^{-\kappa}\le\sigma_i(A)$ for all $i$ (careful: the moderate definition is a lower bound for ALL $i$; show the $o(i^{-\kappa})$ decay violates it for every finite $\kappa$).
(b) *Justify the severe/exponential label.* Show $\limsup_{i\to\infty}\tfrac1i\log\big(1/\sigma_i(A)\big)>0$ (indeed $=+\infty$ per the numerics), so the decay is at least exponential, placing the problem firmly in the severely ill-posed regime.

**Conclusion to state:** $Ax=y$ is **severely (exponentially, in fact super-exponentially) ill-posed**, not moderately ill-posed.

**Difficulty:** moderate, contingent on the crux lemma.
